AccountsResponse.title: AccountsResponse
AccountsResponse.description:
The signed-in person's accounts, oldest first. `discord_linking` is whether linking a Discord account is set up
here; false, `start_discord_link` answers 503.

ActionIds.title: ActionIds
ActionIds.description: The `ids` picked for one `action` of an entity-per-action setting.

ActionListField.title: ActionListField
ActionListField.description: A list of the service's actions, picked from those of `domains`.

AddPieceRequest.title: AddPieceRequest
AddPieceRequest.description: Add a piece of `kind` last on the bench. Its id is the command's `seq`.

AgreeReply.title: AgreeReply
AgreeReply.description:
What agreeing did: `agreed`, what became of each held call, also kept on the agreeing turn in `conversation_id`
(`ChatConversationTurn.agreed`). No turn of hers is stored.

AgreeRequest.title: AgreeRequest
AgreeRequest.description:
The tap on a held receipt's Agree button: `proposal_id`, the `agree` of the turn whose receipts hold it, or the one
a push notification carried.

ApiKeyConnectionRequest.title: ApiKeyConnectionRequest
ApiKeyConnectionRequest.description:
Replace a connection of a kind whose `secret_field` is `api_key` (Sure): `base_url` is the address it is served
at; `api_key` is a key made in the service's own settings, checked against it before anything is stored.

Applied.title: Applied
Applied.description: Whether the event changed an account: false for a Proton user no connection holds.

ArchivePieceRequest.title: ArchivePieceRequest
ArchivePieceRequest.description: Put piece `piece_id` on the bench's shelf: it leaves the layout and the `max_pieces` count, kept whole.

BenchDetail.title: BenchDetail
BenchDetail.description:
A bench as a screen shows it: the bench, its pieces in order, and its latest commands, oldest first.
`undo_next` is the `seq` an Undo should name now (one of `recent`'s), null when there is nothing to undo. `shelf`
is its archived pieces, the most recently archived first: off the layout, not counted toward `max_pieces`, each
kept whole with its last run, to restore.

BenchList.title: BenchList
BenchList.description:
Some of the signed-in person's benches: the open ones, the most recently opened first (`GET /api/benches`), or
the closed ones, the most recently closed first (`GET /api/benches/closed`).

BenchMessage.title: BenchMessage
BenchMessage.description:
A message on a bench's talk: `text` as `ChatRequest`, and `piece_id` when the person just put a paste on the
bench as that piece (a document of theirs), which she is told of with the message.

BenchPiece.title: BenchPiece
BenchPiece.description:
One piece of a bench, on its layout or its shelf. `id` is the `seq` of the command that added it. `piece_version` rises by one with every
change to its title or body; an edit names the version it was based on (`base_version`). `placement` is where it
sits (on the shelf, where it sat when archived). `changed_by` is the `seq` of the last command
that added, edited, moved, archived or restored it, and `changed_at` and `changed_author` (`changed_person_id` for a person's, null
for hers) are when that command was decided and who made it, however long ago. `last_run` is the piece's latest
run, whoever ran it, null for a piece never run. `automation` is an automation piece's installing into Home
Assistant (null for any other kind). `video` is a video piece's video, understood (null for any other kind, and
for a video piece with no body yet). `reader` is a reader piece's page, understood (null for any other kind, and for
a reader piece with no body yet), and `pointer` its highlight (null for none, or once the piece has changed since).
`file` is an image or file piece's bytes, understood, with a short-lived link to them (null for any other kind).
`site` is a site piece's address, measured (null for any other kind, and for a site piece with no address yet).
`recipe` is a recipe piece's recipe, scaled for its headcount (null for any other kind, and for an empty body).

BenchRequest.title: BenchRequest
BenchRequest.description:
A bench to open, by a `title` (1 to `title_max_chars` characters, not only whitespace), an `ask` (what the person
wants to work on: 1 to 4000 characters, not only whitespace, sent to her as their first message in the bench's
talk, which she answers), or both. With only an ask, the title is cut from it until she names the bench; with only
a title, no message is sent.

BenchSummary.title: BenchSummary
BenchSummary.description:
One of the signed-in person's benches. `closed_at` is null while it is open. `piece_count` is the pieces on its
layout now, its shelf not counted; `last_changed_at` is when its last accepted command was decided (a cue of a video's player or a highlight is not one),
null for a bench nothing was done on.
`thread` is the thread its talk is carried on, which a `LiveTurn` names when the talk got a turn.

CatalogueActionInfo.title: CatalogueActionInfo
CatalogueActionInfo.description:
An action the service offers (`domain.name`). `looks_up_only`: the service itself says it only returns data and
changes nothing.

CatalogueEntityInfo.title: CatalogueEntityInfo
CatalogueEntityInfo.description: A thing the service has: `entity_id` (`domain.object_id`), `name` to show, its `domain` and `device_class`.

ChatAttachment.title: ChatAttachment
ChatAttachment.description:
A block of text a person pasted with a message: `text`, 1 to 20000 characters and not only whitespace, and a
`title` of up to 120 characters when it has one. It is her to read in full, beside the message and never in place
of it.

ChatConversation.title: ChatConversation
ChatConversation.description:
The conversation a web thread carries (a person's own, or the kiosk's), oldest turn first, while it is open or
idle. Once it has closed, or before the first message, `conversation_id` and `started_at` are null and `turns` is
empty: the next message starts a new one. `thread` is the web thread, which a `LiveTurn` names when it got a turn.

ChatConversationTurn.title: ChatConversationTurn
ChatConversationTurn.description:
A turn of a conversation a web thread carries. `runs` are the scripts she ran to answer, in the order they ran,
on her turn that is the final answer to the person's message that asked for them (not on a held line before it);
empty on every other turn. `looks` are the pictures of a bench she was given, placed the same way. `working` is
true on the person's turn still owed its answer while her work on it is in flight (a runner has it, or a resumed
one will), so a page shows her still on it rather than the message missed; false on every other turn. `agree` is
the id of the held proposal (`POST /api/chat/agree`) on her turn whose receipts hold it, while the person
reading can still agree to it; null on every other turn, and on a conversation read for another thread than the
person's own. `voiced` is true on her turn that has a voice stored (`Turn.spoken`). `receipts` is what code
stored beside her words on that turn, whether or not `agree` is still offered. `agreed` is what became of the held
calls a person's agreeing turn carried out, shown beside that turn; null on every other turn.

ChatLook.title: ChatLook
ChatLook.description:
A picture she was given of a bench for a message, as the page shows it under her answer: of piece `piece_id`
of bench `bench_id`, or of the whole bench when `piece_id` is null. `url` is a link to the picture (same site, no
session needed) that stops working at `expires_at` (Unix seconds), so a page that stays open reads the
conversation again before then; null when this process mints no links.

ChatMessage.title: ChatMessage
ChatMessage.description:
A message on the person's own web thread: `text` as `ChatRequest`, and the `attachment` they pasted with it,
which is kept with their turn and shown folded under it. `said_aloud` says the words came from the page's record
button (tap to talk), which offers her to answer aloud (`channels.aloud`).

ChatReply.title: ChatReply
ChatReply.description:
Her reply on a web thread, as text. `follows` is true when it only says she will check, or, with an empty `body`,
when her turn is still being worked on elsewhere: the answer is stored as her turn later, announced on
`GET /api/live` as a `LiveTurn` for the thread; on the kiosk it is announced to the device's screen on
`GET /api/kiosk/live`. `receipts` is what code shows beside her words after a turn that did or held changes.

ChatRun.title: ChatRun
ChatRun.description:
One script she ran for a message, as the page shows it under her answer. `result` is `ran` (then `exit_code`
is the script's status, non-zero included), `timed_out` (stopped at its deadline; what it printed is kept),
`out_of_memory`, `failed` (nothing readable came back) or `unknown` (the pod was made but what became of it could
not be learned; the script may have run); it is null for a run with no recorded result (still going, or its runner
stopped). `stdout` and `stderr` are empty until there is a result, and `cut` says one was cut to the sandbox's
limit. `made` are the text files it left, `skipped` the names of those left out.

ChatRunFile.title: ChatRunFile
ChatRunFile.description: A text file a run left in its working directory.

ClearHighlightRequest.title: ClearHighlightRequest
ClearHighlightRequest.description:
Take the highlight off reader piece `piece_id`, as it is at `base_version` (a `Point` with no passage). Refused
`not_reader` for any other piece and `stale_base` when it has changed since.

CommandApplied.title: CommandApplied
CommandApplied.description:
The command was accepted as `seq`; `piece_id` is the piece it changed (for an add, the new piece), null for a
change of the bench itself (an undo of a rename).

CommandRefused.title: CommandRefused
CommandRefused.description:
The command was refused as `seq` and logged so; nothing on the bench changed. `reason` is why, a stable word a
client branches on (`stale_base`: read the bench again and redo the edit on the newer version).

CommandRequest.title: CommandRequest
CommandRequest.description: One change to a bench, told apart by `type`.

ConnectionCatalogue.title: ConnectionCatalogue
ConnectionCatalogue.description:
What the connection's service has now for a setting to pick from, read live at `read_at`, narrowed to `domains`
when asked.

ConnectionChange.title: ConnectionChange
ConnectionChange.description:
`PATCH /api/connections/{id}`: either the new `label`, or the new `holder`: `household` hands the connection to
the household, `person` takes back one the signed-in person handed over. Exactly one of them.

ConnectionKindInfo.title: ConnectionKindInfo
ConnectionKindInfo.description:
A kind of connection a household or person can make, as its adapter declares it: what the panel shows for it
and what the request must carry. `name` is the `kind` of a new connection; `most` is how many of it one owner may hold; `title` and `what` label it; `blurb`,
`connected` and `removed` are what the panel says before and after; `holders` is who may hold one, the household,
a person (`person`) or either, and a new connection of a kind a person may hold is theirs until they hand it over;
`takes_address` whether a person types its address (`address_placeholder` shows the shape); `secret_field` is the
request field that carries the key or token, `secret_label` what to call it to a person and `secret_noun` its
name in a button. `connect` is how it is connected: `pasted`, a person types the secret, or `oauth`, through the
service's own consent screen (`POST /api/connections/oauth/{provider}/start`), or `bridge`, a login to the service's account
made once from the room (`POST /api/mail-bridge/login`); `set_up` is whether this app can
connect it at all (an OAuth kind whose client is not configured is not); `has_settings` whether a person sets anything on a connection of
it (`GET /api/connections/{id}/settings`).

ConnectionRefused.title: ConnectionRefused
ConnectionRefused.description:
Why a connection was not stored; nothing was. `reason`: `bad_url`, the address is not one the service may be
reached at (a scheme the kind allows, a host, no credentials, query or fragment); `key_refused`, the service turned
the key or token away; `unreachable`, nothing answered there in time, or it redirected or failed; `wrong_service`,
what answered is not that service's API. `detail` is the kind's own words for a person.

ConnectionResource.title: ConnectionResource
ConnectionResource.description:
What a connection reaches, as its service names it: `ref` is the service's own id (a mailbox's address) and
addresses it, `kind` what it is (`mailbox`), `name` what to show. `shared` says the household may use it; false,
only the connection's owner may.

ConnectionSettings.title: ConnectionSettings
ConnectionSettings.description:
A connection's settings. `revision` counts the writes, 0 for a connection never set, and is what the next write
must carry; `updated_at` and `updated_by` say who wrote them last (null for a connection never set, and `updated_by`
null once the person is gone).

ConnectionSettingsRequest.title: ConnectionSettingsRequest
ConnectionSettingsRequest.description: The whole of a connection's settings, replacing what is stored, and the `revision` they were read at.

ConnectionsResponse.title: ConnectionsResponse
ConnectionsResponse.description:
The signed-in person's household's connections, by kind, and every kind that can be connected, in the order to
show them. `can_connect` is whether this app holds the key that seals them; false, none can be added and
`connections` is empty.

ControlsRefused.title: ControlsRefused
ControlsRefused.description:
Why the controls were not stored; nothing was. `reason`: `too_many`; `bad_label`, a label of 1 to 40
characters is wanted; `bad_id`, a name outside `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`; `duplicate_id`, a name is used twice;
`unknown_entity`, a light the house's catalogue does not have, or one the action does not suit; `full`, the screen
holds as many pieces as it can; `already_shown`, `required`, which a screen's layout rules refuse.

CorrectionRequest.title: CorrectionRequest
CorrectionRequest.description:
What the fact should say now: `text`, 1 to 1000 characters and not only whitespace, one statement true on its
own. `visibility`, when given, is who may know it from now on; only the fact's owner may change it. The kind,
who it is about and whose it is carry over.

DeviceControl.title: DeviceControl
DeviceControl.description:
One control as stored: `name` its stable key on the device, `label` what its button says, `entity_id` the light or
scene the house calls it, which `action` turns on or off (a scene only on).

DeviceControlList.title: DeviceControlList
DeviceControlList.description:
A device's touch controls in the order its screen shows them; empty when it has none. `piece_version` is the controls
piece's version, which an edit names as `base_version`: 0 while the screen has no controls piece or has not been laid
out.

DeviceControlWanted.title: DeviceControlWanted
DeviceControlWanted.description:
One control asked for: `name` is the key of a control already on the device, null for a new one, which is given a
key from its label.

DeviceControlsRequest.title: DeviceControlsRequest
DeviceControlsRequest.description:
The whole list a device is to show: it replaces what it had, if the list is still at `base_version`, the `piece_version`
last read.

DevicesResponse.title: DevicesResponse
DevicesResponse.description: The signed-in person's household's unrevoked devices, oldest first.

EditPieceRequest.title: EditPieceRequest
EditPieceRequest.description:
Replace piece `piece_id`'s title and body, based on its `base_version`; refused `stale_base` when another change
came first, and nothing is merged.

EntityListField.title: EntityListField
EntityListField.description: A list of the service's entities, picked from those of `domains` (any domain when empty).

EntityPerActionField.title: EntityPerActionField
EntityPerActionField.description: For each of `for_actions`, a list of entities picked from those of `domains`.

ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse
ErrorResponse.description:
The body of every error a route declares. `code` is a stable machine-readable word a client branches on;
`detail` is for a person and carries no data.

FactSource.title: FactSource
FactSource.description:
Where a fact was learned. `took_part` is whether the person reading was in that conversation. `channel` is
what the conversation started on and `place` where, when the channel is a shared device; each is null when not
recorded (conversations from before, or a channel with no place). A correction made on the web is a `command`
conversation of its own on the `web` channel, with the reader taking part.

ForgetResponse.title: ForgetResponse
ForgetResponse.description: How many facts were deleted: the one forgotten and every earlier version it replaced. None of them is kept.

HealthResponse.title: HealthResponse
HealthResponse.description: The process is up. Says nothing about the database.

Heartbeat.title: Heartbeat
Heartbeat.description: The pod of `epoch` is alive, with the SHA-256 (hex) of the TLS certificate Bridge serves IMAP and SMTP under.

HouseholdConnection.title: HouseholdConnection
HouseholdConnection.description:
One of the household's connections. `id` is what addresses it; `label` is what its owner calls it, empty for one
never named. `kind` is the service, the `name` of a registered connection kind; `base_url` where it is
reached; `added_by` the person who added it, null once they are not among the household's people or for one
carried over from her own setup; `personal` whether it is the signed-in person's own (a code host) and not the
household's; `checked_at` when the service last answered with it, at its adding or on one of
her reads since. `needs` is set while its person must act before it works again (`reconnect`: the service
refused its grant, so connect it again); `scopes` are what an OAuth service granted and `missing_scopes` what its kind asks for
that it did not (a person unticked them), empty for a pasted kind. `resources` is what it reaches, each shared or
kept (none for a kind that lists none). `can_hand_over` says the signed-in person may hand it to the household
(it is theirs and its kind allows the household to hold it); `can_take_back` that they may take it back (they
added it and its kind allows a person to hold it).

InstallPieceRequest.title: InstallPieceRequest
InstallPieceRequest.description:
Approve her proposal `proposal` (`automation.install_proposal.seq` of piece `piece_id`): install the piece into Home
Assistant as she proposed. Refused `no_proposal` when that is not the piece's proposal or was installed already,
`stale_base` when the piece changed since. Answered once the house has been written to; how that went is the
piece's `automation.last_install`.

InstallProposal.title: InstallProposal
InstallProposal.description:
Her proposal `seq` to install the piece as it is at `piece_version`: `enabled` or not once installed, turning off
`turn_off` (an automation's entity id) with it, null for none. The person approves it with an `install` command
naming `seq`.

InstallState.title: InstallState
InstallState.description:
What the latest install of the piece, or undo of one, did to the house. `seq` is its command; `action`
`install` or `uninstall`; `automation_id` the id it is installed under in Home Assistant, the same for every
install of the piece; for an install, `enabled` as chosen (null for an uninstall) and `turn_off` the automation
it turned off (an uninstall's, the one it turned back on). `install_ending` is null while it runs, and for good
when its runner stopped part way (it is never carried out again; check the house); `done`; `refused` (Home
Assistant refused the config, `install_note` its reason; nothing was written) or `failed` (`install_note` says
from which step, and whether anything may have changed).

JobCancelled.title: JobCancelled
JobCancelled.description: The job after the cancel: `state` is `cancelled`, or what it had already ended as.

KeeperEvent.title: KeeperEvent
KeeperEvent.description:
What Bridge reported about one Proton account (`user_id`), in `epoch`: its `state`, or a `sync` event with its
`progress` (0 to 1) for a `progress` event. Exactly one of `state` and `sync`.

KeeperVault.title: KeeperVault
KeeperVault.description:
What the keeper starts Bridge from: the `generation` it must hold in its next write-back, and the vault and
keychain as base64, both null before the first write-back.

KioskControl.title: KioskControl
KioskControl.description: One touch control: `name` is its stable key, `label` what its button says.

KioskControlDone.title: KioskControlDone
KioskControlDone.description: Whether her tool reported the control carried out (`done`); false when the tool or the house refused it.

KioskControls.title: KioskControls
KioskControls.description: The kiosk's touch controls, in the order they are shown; empty when none are set.

KioskDevice.title: KioskDevice
KioskDevice.description: The device a kiosk browser is paired as: never a person. `place` is where it stands (`hallway`).

KioskGlance.title: KioskGlance
KioskGlance.description:
What the kiosk shows at a glance, shared things only. `home` is the first names of the household's people who
are home: empty when everyone known is away, null when it cannot be known. `not_connected` names the glance's
sources that have nothing behind them yet, which the page shows as not connected, never with sample data.

KioskLayout.title: KioskLayout
KioskLayout.description:
The device's screen as it is laid out. `laid_out` is false while nothing has changed it, and the page then shows its
fixed layout; `seq` is the last change's number, 0 when not laid out; `placed` are the pieces in order.

KioskMessage.title: KioskMessage
KioskMessage.description:
A message on the kiosk's thread: `text` as `ChatRequest`. `said_aloud` says the words came from the page's record
button (tap to talk), which offers her to answer aloud (`channels.aloud`).

KioskPairRequest.title: KioskPairRequest
KioskPairRequest.description: A device token from `python -m ashley.channels.devices add`, pasted once on the tablet to pair it.

KioskPiece.title: KioskPiece
KioskPiece.description:
One piece of the screen: `id` its stable key, `kind` what it is (`clock`, `home`, `conversation`, `controls`),
`order` its place among the pieces (0 first, no gaps) and `size` how much of the row it takes (`small` a quarter,
`medium` a half, `large` three quarters, `full` the row).

LexiconRefused.title: LexiconRefused
LexiconRefused.description:
Why `refused_for` a word was not stored: `not_a_word` (the path is not one word-like token), `blank_spelling`,
`too_long` (the word or its spelling is over 64 characters) or `full` (the household holds the most it may).

LexiconWord.title: LexiconWord
LexiconWord.description:
`real` is the word as written, `spoken` the spelling the voice says right. `edited_by` is the person who last set
it, null once they are gone.

LexiconWordRequest.title: LexiconWordRequest
LexiconWordRequest.description: The spelling to say for the word in the path.

LexiconWords.title: LexiconWords
LexiconWords.description: The signed-in person's household's words by `real`, and the most it holds.

LinkStartResponse.title: LinkStartResponse
LinkStartResponse.description:
Where to send this browser to link a Discord account: Discord's authorization page, which returns it to
`/connections?link=<outcome>`. Good for one link, within sign-in's `pending_minutes`.

LinkedAccount.title: LinkedAccount
LinkedAccount.description:
One of the signed-in person's accounts elsewhere. `system` names where (`authentik`, `discord`,
`home_assistant`); `handle` is the account's name there as it was when they linked it themselves, null when the
admin mapped it. `unlinkable` is whether they may unlink it here, which only a Discord account is: unlinking the
account they sign in with would sign them out for good.

ListedDevice.title: ListedDevice
ListedDevice.description:
One of the household's devices. `form` is what it is wired to, not what it is called: a voice `satellite`, a
household's `discord_server`, the household's Home Assistant (`household`, which hands in wakes), or `other` (the hallway
tablet is one). `audience` is who hears or reads what it
says and `medium` how it reaches them. Never a token, host or server id.

LiveBench.title: LiveBench
LiveBench.description: Command `seq` changed bench `bench_id`, one of this person's own: a page showing it reads the bench back.

LiveCue.title: LiveCue
LiveCue.description:
She cued the player of video piece `piece_id` on this person's bench `bench_id`: `play`, `pause`, or `seek` to
`seconds`. Heard only by the screens open now; a page showing the piece drives its player and reads nothing back.

LiveEvent.title: LiveEvent
LiveEvent.description: One event on `GET /api/live`, the JSON of one `data:` line, told apart by `type`.

LiveFailed.title: LiveFailed
LiveFailed.description:
A turn on `thread`, one of this person's own, ended with no reply after its request had returned pending (an
empty `ChatReply.body` with `follows`): a page showing it shows the person's last message as unanswered, `why`
as the request would have said (`unavailable` a 503, `refused` a 422); `retrying` it failed and its work is kept to try
again, `unfinished` it failed with nothing she could say, `too_big` the work was too big for one reply and is not
tried again: the page words each and no turn of hers carries them.

LivePage.title: LivePage
LivePage.description:
She moved this person's page to `room`, and to bench `bench_id` in the workshop when it is set: each of their
open pages flies there, or, while the person is in the middle of something, offers to follow her.

LiveResync.title: LiveResync
LiveResync.description:
Something may have been missed (the feed reconnected, or this stream fell behind): read back what is shown, and
forget the turns heard so far.

LiveScreen.title: LiveScreen
LiveScreen.description:
Command `seq` changed the screen of device `device_id`, one of the household's: a tablet showing that screen reads
its layout back, and the Devices room its buttons.

LiveState.title: LiveState
LiveState.description:
Her state in one turn on a channel this person may see: their own (a DM, their web chat) or a shared one (a
satellite, a shared Discord channel), never which room or who is talking. `turn` is a random token naming the
turn. A screen shows her `listening`, `thinking` or `speaking` while any turn it heard is, until that turn's `idle` or
`at_most_s` after it heard the state, whichever is first.

LiveTurn.title: LiveTurn
LiveTurn.description:
A turn was stored on `thread`, one of this person's own threads (`ChatConversation.thread` names the web one):
a page showing it reads the conversation back.

LoggedCommand.title: LoggedCommand
LoggedCommand.description:
One command of a bench's log: `seq`, when it was decided, who made it (`author`, and `person_id` for a
person's, null for hers), its `type`, `outcome` `accepted` or the refusal's reason, and `piece_id`, the piece it
changed (null when refused). Never the text it carried.

LookPage.title: LookPage
LookPage.description:
What the page a browser pod photographs reads (`GET /api/look/{token}`): the bench as its owner sees it, or one
piece of it, and the kinds the page needs to draw a piece, which the session-only kinds route would not give it.

MeResponse.title: MeResponse
MeResponse.description: Who this browser is signed in as.

MemoryFact.title: MemoryFact
MemoryFact.description:
A current fact that concerns the signed-in person: about them, theirs (`owner`), or the household's (`about`
and `owner` both null). `valid_from` is when it became true to her, so "new this week" is a filter on it.
`standing` facts reach every reply; the rest come back when a message bears on them. `replaced` is the fact this
one superseded, when there was one the reader may see.

MemoryFactsResponse.title: MemoryFactsResponse
MemoryFactsResponse.description:
Every current fact that concerns the signed-in person, newest `valid_from` first. Never another person's
private fact, even one about the reader.

MessageRequest.title: MessageRequest
MessageRequest.description:
What a device heard or was sent. `text` is 1 to 4000 characters and not only whitespace. `thread`, when given,
is 1 to 64 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, the device's own name for a conversation it keeps apart from its others.

MessageResponse.title: MessageResponse
MessageResponse.description:
Her reply. `body` is rendered for `medium`, the device's: for `spoken`, plain sentences to hand a TTS engine. It
holds only her words; `receipts` is what code shows beside them, which a device that speaks says none of.

MovePieceRequest.title: MovePieceRequest
MovePieceRequest.description: Put piece `piece_id` at `placement`, an order among the pieces as they stand (the others shift).

MoveRequest.title: MoveRequest
MoveRequest.description:
Whose the fact is from now on: `household` makes it the household's (about and owner become null, and it is
shared), allowed to the person who owns it when it is about them or about the household; `mine` makes a household
fact theirs (owner becomes them). The text and kind carry over.

NewApiKeyConnectionRequest.title: NewApiKeyConnectionRequest
NewApiKeyConnectionRequest.description: A new connection of the registered `kind`, called `label`, with an `api_key`.

NewTokenConnectionRequest.title: NewTokenConnectionRequest
NewTokenConnectionRequest.description: A new connection of the registered `kind`, called `label`, with a `token`.

OAuthStartRequest.title: OAuthStartRequest
OAuthStartRequest.description:
Start connecting an OAuth `kind` under `label`, held by `holder`: the household's or the person's own, as the
kind allows (`ConnectionKindInfo.holders`).

OAuthStartResponse.title: OAuthStartResponse
OAuthStartResponse.description:
Where to send this browser to connect: the service's consent page, which returns it to
`/connections?connect=<outcome>`. Good for one connect, within sign-in's `pending_minutes`.

PastConversation.title: PastConversation
PastConversation.description: An earlier conversation with its turns, oldest first.

PastHistory.title: PastHistory
PastHistory.description:
A page of `PastSummary`, newest activity first. `next` is the `before` that reads the following page, null on
the last.

PastSummary.title: PastSummary
PastSummary.description:
One conversation the signed-in person took part in, on any channel. `channel` is what it started on and `place`
where, when the channel is a shared device; each is null when not recorded (conversations from before, or a
channel with no place). `state` is as of the read.

PastTurn.title: PastTurn
PastTurn.description:
A turn of an earlier conversation. `speaker` is the first name the household knows the person by who said it,
the household's name on its own turn, null for her turns and a speaker no one identified.

Person.title: Person
Person.description: One person of a household, as they are known to her. `name` is theirs to see; it is never logged.

PieceAutomation.title: PieceAutomation
PieceAutomation.description:
An automation piece's installing: `install_proposal` waiting on the person's approval (null when none is, or the
piece changed since it was made), and `last_install`, what the latest install or undo of one did (null for a piece
never installed).

PieceFile.title: PieceFile
PieceFile.description:
An `image` or `file` piece's bytes, understood: the file's `name`, `size_bytes` and `media_type`. `url` is a
link to the bytes (same site, no session needed) that stops working at `expires_at` (Unix seconds), so a page that
stays open reads the bench again before then; null when this process mints no links. `image` says the page may
show it in place; any file may be saved from `url`.

PieceKind.title: PieceKind
PieceKind.description:
One kind of piece, from `kinds.json`. `family` `stored`: the body is the content; `live`: the body is a
reference to a source the client renders. `max_chars` is the longest body a piece of it may have. `format` is how a
stored body is written: `markdown`, `plain` (shown as typed), `code`, whose `language` names it (null otherwise),
`automation`, Home Assistant's automation config as a JSON object (`alias`, `description`, `triggers`,
`conditions`, `actions`, `mode`; an empty body is a draft), `site`, one https URL, or `video`, a JSON object of
a `url` (a YouTube or Vimeo page, or a direct media file) and an optional `start` in seconds. A `live` kind's
body is a reference, shown in a frame.

PiecePlace.title: PiecePlace
PiecePlace.description:
Where a piece sits: `order` among the bench's pieces (0 first; a bench's pieces hold exactly 0 to n-1) and its
size class.

PiecePointer.title: PiecePointer
PiecePointer.description:
The passage of a reader piece she highlighted: characters `start` up to `end` (Unicode code points) of paragraph
`paragraph`. `seq` is the command that put it up, so a screen can tell a highlight it has already brought into
view from a new one. Null when there is none, or the piece has changed since it was put up.

PieceReader.title: PieceReader
PieceReader.description:
A reader piece's page, understood: where it came from (`url`, https), its own `title` (may be empty), and its
`paragraphs` in order, which are what a passage's `paragraph` indexes. `recording` is set on a transcript.

PieceRecipe.title: PieceRecipe
PieceRecipe.description:
A recipe piece's recipe: where it was published (`url`, https), its `name`, how much it makes as the page says
(`yield_text`) and as a count (`makes`, null when that names no number), the headcount it is for (`serves`, null:
as written) and what every amount was multiplied by (`factor`, null when nothing was scaled), the minutes it takes
(each null when the page gives none), its ingredient lines and its steps as the page wrote them.

PieceRecording.title: PieceRecording
PieceRecording.description:
What a transcript was made from: the bench piece `piece_id` (a clip or audio piece) and the second each of the
reader's paragraphs starts at (`starts[i]` for `paragraphs[i]`).

PieceRun.title: PieceRun
PieceRun.description:
A piece's run: `run_id`, the `piece_version` it ran, when it started and finished, and its `run_output`, null
until it is recorded: while it runs, and for good when its runner stopped part way (it is never run again).

PieceSite.title: PieceSite
PieceSite.description:
A site piece's address, measured. `frameable` is true when the site lets a page frame it, false when it refused
(an `X-Frame-Options` of DENY or SAMEORIGIN, a `frame-ancestors` that leaves this page out, or a non-2xx answer), and
null when it is not known (not measured yet, or the site did not answer): a screen shows it as it would a site that
may or may not frame. `title` is the page's own, empty when none was read.

PieceVideo.title: PieceVideo
PieceVideo.description:
A video piece's video: its `provider` (`youtube`, `vimeo`, or `file` for a direct media file), the `url` as
written, the `embed_url` to frame (a `file`'s is its own url, to play in a video element) with the start already in
it, and `start`, where it begins in whole seconds. A site's url is its body.

ProtonAccount.title: ProtonAccount
ProtonAccount.description:
A Proton account of a connection the signed-in person can see. `state` is Bridge's; `syncing` is true while Bridge
serves its mailbox empty, with the last `sync_progress` it reported (0 to 1, null before any).

ProtonLoginRefused.title: ProtonLoginRefused
ProtonLoginRefused.description:
Why Bridge or the app refused a step: `credentials` (username or password), `code` (the two-factor code),
`mailbox_password`, `paid_plan` (Bridge needs a paid Proton plan), `connection` (Bridge could not reach Proton),
`aborted` (Bridge ended the login), `verification` (the human check did not pass), `security_key` (the account's
two-factor is a hardware key only), `label_taken`, `too_many`, or `other`. The login is over; the person starts
again.

ProtonLoginStart.title: ProtonLoginStart
ProtonLoginStart.description:
First step of a login from the room: the connection's `label` (as any connection's) and the Proton username and
password, which go to Bridge once and are kept nowhere.

ProtonLoginStep.title: ProtonLoginStep
ProtonLoginStep.description:
Where a login stands. `step` is what the person is asked for next (`two_factor`, `mailbox_password`),
`human_verification` (Proton wants to check it is a person: they open `verification_url`, an https page on proton.me,
in their own browser, then send the password again as verified) or `connected`, when `connection_id` is the stored
connection and `addresses` the mail addresses it reaches.

ProtonMailboxPassword.title: ProtonMailboxPassword
ProtonMailboxPassword.description: The mailbox password of an account that has two, with the `label` the login began under.

ProtonSecondFactor.title: ProtonSecondFactor
ProtonSecondFactor.description: The two-factor `code`, with the `label` the login began under.

ProtonVerifiedLogin.title: ProtonVerifiedLogin
ProtonVerifiedLogin.description: The password again, with the `label` the login began under, once the person has passed Proton's human check.

PushEndpointRequest.title: PushEndpointRequest
PushEndpointRequest.description: Which browser: its push subscription's endpoint.

PushKeyResponse.title: PushKeyResponse
PushKeyResponse.description: Her VAPID public key, base64url: the `applicationServerKey` a browser subscribes with.

PushKeys.title: PushKeys
PushKeys.description: The browser's keys for what is pushed to it, base64url, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives them.

PushStateResponse.title: PushStateResponse
PushStateResponse.description:
The signed-in person's notifications: how many browsers they have subscribed, and whether the one asking is
one of them.

PushSubscriptionRequest.title: PushSubscriptionRequest
PushSubscriptionRequest.description:
This browser's push subscription, as `PushSubscription.toJSON()` gives it; extra fields it may carry
(`expirationTime`) are ignored.

ReadyResponse.title: ReadyResponse
ReadyResponse.description: A database connection could be opened. `writable` is false on a standby, which can serve reads only.

RecipeLine.title: RecipeLine
RecipeLine.description:
One ingredient line: `text` as the page wrote it, `shown` with its amount scaled (equal to `text` when it was
not). `amount` and `amount_max` (a range's top) are the page's numbers in `unit` (a unit key of the server's units,
null for a count or for a line with no amount); `scaled` says whether `shown` was multiplied.

RememberRequest.title: RememberRequest
RememberRequest.description:
A line to remember now: turn `turn_id` of conversation `conversation_id`, one the signed-in person took part
in, either author's.

RememberResponse.title: RememberResponse
RememberResponse.description:
What remembering the line changed. `facts` are the facts she learned from it, and from any earlier lines of
that conversation she had not learned from yet, that concern the reader, in the order she decided them, each with `replaced` when it updated an older one; `unseen` how many more she learned that
the reader may not see; `ended` how many facts she knew stopped being current. All empty and zero: nothing new.

Reminder.title: Reminder
Reminder.description:
A reminder still to fire: for `person`, set by `made_by` (often the same person), what it says, when it fires
next (`due_at`, and `local_at`, that time as the household's wall clock, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`), and how it repeats:
`repeat` none for once, else every `every` days, weeks, months or years. `what` is the person's own, shown only to
them and to whoever set it. `state`: `scheduled`, still to fire; `sending`, fired and its push not tried yet;
`undelivered`, fired but no push reached their phone yet (it is tried again for a day, and her words are in
their conversation history); `failed`, it could not fire. A fired one stays listed until it is delivered or the
person dismisses it. `on_deposit` is, for a reminder that waits on a deposit instead of a time, the rule in words
(it fires on every match until cancelled, and `due_at` is when it was set); None for a timed one.

ReminderCancelled.title: ReminderCancelled
ReminderCancelled.description:
The reminder cancelled, so a repeating one fires no more, or, for one that already fired and is listed
undelivered or failed, dismissed from the list.

RemindersResponse.title: RemindersResponse
RemindersResponse.description: The signed-in person's reminders, for them or set by them, soonest first.

ReplacedFact.title: ReplacedFact
ReplacedFact.description: The fact this one superseded: what it said, and when it stopped being true.

ReportCheck.title: ReportCheck
ReportCheck.description:
A comparison the script made of a number it measured on the geometry: `actual op target` within `tolerance`, resting
on the measurements `rests_on`. `verdict` is computed by the app: `pass`, `fail`, or `unconfirmed` when it would pass
but a measurement it rests on is guessed or missing from the run; any other source confirms.

ReportIsland.title: ReportIsland
ReportIsland.description:
Overhang faces of a part that join up: the corners of their box (mm, x y z), the bed area support under them covers
(`area_mm2`), and the gap straight down to the part below or the bed, smallest and median by area (mm).

ReportOverlap.title: ReportOverlap
ReportOverlap.description:
Two shown parts, `a` and `b`, that occupy the same space: the `volume_mm3` they share and the corners of the box
around it (mm, x y z). Each is also a failed `parts_apart` check.

ReportPart.title: ReportPart
ReportPart.description:
One part's `volume` (mm³) and the corners of its bounding box (mm, x y z). `role` is what the script said the part
is for, one of the roles in the print settings (`reference` is the real object modelled for fit, which is never
printed), or `unknown` when it said nothing. `form` is the measurements choice row a `reference` part names as what
kind of thing it stands in for, null on every other part.

ReportPrint.title: ReportPrint
ReportPrint.description:
The print check of the parts as modelled, flat on the bed. `skip_reason` says why nothing was checked, and `printed` is
then empty: `no_settings` (the run had no print settings), `too_many_triangles` (the model is over `max_triangles`)
or `no_printed_parts` (every part is a `reference`). `bed_fit_skipped` is `no_bed` when no bed size is known. A gap
too small to print open or to pull support out of is a failed check, `print_gap:<part>` or
`print_trapped_support:<part>`, among the report's checks.

ReportPrintPart.title: ReportPrintPart
ReportPrintPart.description:
What the print check found on one printed part, checked alone on its own bed at its lowest Z (`bed_z`, mm): the
bed area its support covers (`support_area_mm2`, which is
information, never a failure), the area lying on the bed (`bed_contact_mm2`), `fits_bed` (null when no bed size is
known), and its overhang `islands`, the smallest gap first, the first few of `islands_total`.

ResourceShare.title: ResourceShare
ResourceShare.description:
`PATCH /api/connections/{id}/resources/{ref}`: `shared` true shares the resource with the household, false keeps
it for the connection's owner.

RestorePieceRequest.title: RestorePieceRequest
RestorePieceRequest.description:
Bring piece `piece_id` back from the shelf, last on the bench at the size it had; refused `full` when the bench
holds `max_pieces`.

RollbackRequest.title: RollbackRequest
RollbackRequest.description: Roll the skill back to the text of live version `to_version` (0: the seed), as a new version.

RunApplied.title: RunApplied
RunApplied.description:
The Run command was accepted as `seq` and the piece was run as `run_id`: `run_output` is what came out. The
bench read back shows it as the piece's `last_run`.

RunArtifact.title: RunArtifact
RunArtifact.description:
A binary file the run made and kept: its `name` in the working directory, `size_bytes` and `media_type`. `url` is
a download link on this site, no session needed, that stops at `expires_at` (Unix seconds), so a page that stays open
reads the bench again before then; null when this process mints no links.

RunOutput.title: RunOutput
RunOutput.description:
What came out of a run. `run_outcome`: `ran` (to its end; `exit_code` is its status, non-zero included),
`timed_out` (stopped at its deadline; what it printed until then is kept), `out_of_memory`, `failed` (nothing
readable came back; nothing may have run) or `unknown` (it may have run, and what it printed was lost). `stdout`
and `stderr` are cut to the sandbox's limit (`output_cut` says one was); `files` are the text files it left in its
working directory, which the piece's next run starts with when it `ran`; `files_left_out` names the ones not kept.
`artifacts` are the binary files a model run made and kept (empty for any other run), with download links; `report`
is the report a model script wrote, each check judged by the app, null when the run left none.

RunReport.title: RunReport
RunReport.description:
What a model script reported (`out/report.json`), all lengths in millimetres: its parts, the mesh's `triangles`,
its checks and the pairs of parts that `overlaps`. `overlap_parts_skipped` counts the shown parts too many to compare.
`print` is what the print check found, null for a run of a helper that had none.

RunRequest.title: RunRequest
RunRequest.description:
Run piece `piece_id`, a code piece, as it is at `base_version` (the version the screen shows), in
`run_language`, one of `WorkshopKinds.run_languages`.

SettingChange.title: SettingChange
SettingChange.description: One key a write changed: the values themselves are not listed. `edited_by` is null once the person is gone.

SettingChanges.title: SettingChanges
SettingChanges.description: The changes, newest first. `next_before` is the `before` that fetches the page after, null at the end.

SettingEntry.title: SettingEntry
SettingEntry.description:
The value of the setting `key`: `ids` for an entity or action list, `per_action` for an entity-per-action one
(the other is empty). A setting with no entry is empty.

SettingInfo.title: SettingInfo
SettingInfo.description:
One setting a kind declares. `decides` is what it changes in how she behaves: `taint`, `tier` and `read` settings
change what she trusts, asks about or counts as a change; `plain` ones are preferences.

SettingsRefused.title: SettingsRefused

SkillDetail.title: SkillDetail
SkillDetail.description:
A kind's skill as it loads now: `skill_version` is the live version (0: the seed, with `seeded_from` naming the
skill it was adapted from), `edits` how many live versions the household made, `pinned` whether her edits wait
for a person's approval. `waiting` is her newest waiting edit, with its full `waiting_body`. `changelog` is the
latest entries, newest first.

SkillRefusal.title: SkillRefusal
SkillRefusal.description:
A change to a skill was refused and nothing changed. `reason` is a stable word a client branches on: `stale`
(the skill moved on: read it again), `unchanged`, `no_such_version`, `not_proposed`, `bad_note`, `bad_body`,
`unknown_kind`.

SkillVersion.title: SkillVersion
SkillVersion.description:
One entry of a skill's changelog. `status` `live`: it loaded when it was current; `proposed`: her edit of a
pinned skill, waiting for approval; `declined`: a person declined it. `author` is who made it; `restored_from`
is the version a rollback copied (0 is the seed); `base_version` is the live version it was made against.

SpendBalance.title: SpendBalance
SpendBalance.description:
`read`: `quota` as of `read_at`. `failed`: a read was tried at `read_at` and gave nothing. `unknown`: the provider
offers no read, or none is set up here, and `why` says which. `free`: a local model, with nothing to run out of.
`docs_url` is the documentation page for the provider's billing, when there is one.

SpendEstimate.title: SpendEstimate
SpendEstimate.description:
The household's monthly budget less this month's ledger spend: an estimate, not the provider's figure. While
`unpriced_calls` is above 0 the remainder is an upper bound.

SpendProvider.title: SpendProvider
SpendProvider.description:
`kind`: `paid` and `local` as the catalog says, `unlisted` for a provider the ledger holds that the catalog does
not name.

SpendQuota.title: SpendQuota
SpendQuota.description: What the provider itself reports of an account's allowance in the current period, in its own `unit`; not money.

SpendResponse.title: SpendResponse
SpendResponse.description:
Usage as of `as_of`, in the household's time zone `zone` (an IANA name). Providers are the paid ones first, in
catalog order, then any other with calls in the spans, by name.

SpendSpans.title: SpendSpans
SpendSpans.description: The same usage over the three spans.

SpendTask.title: SpendTask
SpendTask.description: One task's share of a provider's usage.

SpendTotals.title: SpendTotals
SpendTotals.description:
Usage over one span. `calls` counts every call, including failed ones; `metered_calls` those that reported
usage; `unpriced_calls` those whose usage has no price, which `cost_usd` leaves out. `cost_usd` is the ledger's:
published list prices times reported usage, null when no call had a price. Speech is billed by `characters` and
`audio_ms`, and its tokens are 0.

SpendWindow.title: SpendWindow
SpendWindow.description: A span's start, an instant: local midnight in the report's zone.

SpokenLimits.title: SpokenLimits
SpokenLimits.description:
Recording stops at `max_ms`, or after `speech_ms` of speech then `silence_ms` of quiet (speech: RMS >= `quiet_rms`).
Her spoken answer to an utterance can be fetched for `voice_s` seconds.

TokenConnectionRequest.title: TokenConnectionRequest
TokenConnectionRequest.description:
Replace a connection of a kind whose `secret_field` is `token` (Home Assistant, GitLab, GitHub): `base_url` is
the address it is served at, left out for a kind that has one address (GitHub's); `token` is the access token,
checked against the service before anything is stored.

Transcript.title: Transcript
Transcript.description:
What was heard in one spoken utterance, in real spellings; empty when nothing was said. The page sends it as a
typed message, so a spoken turn is a typed one on the same thread.

UndoRequest.title: UndoRequest
UndoRequest.description:
Undo command `seq`, while what it changed has not changed since. Refused `nothing_to_undo` when `seq` is an undo
(there is no redo) or older than the bench's last `undo_window` commands, and `changed_since` when it was already
undone. Undoing an install takes it back out of the house before it is answered (`automation.last_install` of the
piece).

VaultWrite.title: VaultWrite
VaultWrite.description: A write-back: the vault and keychain (base64) the keeper read at `generation`, from the pod of `epoch`.

WakeAccepted.title: WakeAccepted
WakeAccepted.description: The wake's id, and `duplicate` when its event id had arrived before and nothing new was stored.

WakeRequest.title: WakeRequest
WakeRequest.description:
One wake from Home Assistant, as `rest_command.ashley_wake` sends it: structured fields only, so free text
cannot arrive here. `event_id` is HA's id for this run of the automation (`{{ context.id }}`), which makes a
retry the same wake; `event` the slug a wake rule answers; `who` the `person.*` entity it is about; `what` a slug
of what it concerns; `when` when it happened, with its offset (now when absent).

WireAgreed.title: WireAgreed
WireAgreed.description:
What became of a held proposal the person agreed to, shown beside their agreeing turn and never as her words:
`carried`, each held call in the order it was held, or `interrupted` true with none when the run stopped partway, so any of
them may or may not have taken effect.

WireAgreedCall.title: WireAgreedCall
WireAgreedCall.description:
One held call the person agreed to: `summary`, code's own words for it as the person was shown it, and whether it
`ran`, `failed` or was `not_run` (not offered where it was agreed). Never what the call returned.

WireReceipt.title: WireReceipt
WireReceipt.description:
One change: `headline` is the tool's plain label, `detail` code's own summary of the call (null where the reply
was shared), `why` the reason it ran or waits, when there is one.

WireReceipts.title: WireReceipts
WireReceipts.description:
The changes that ran without asking (`ran`) and the calls waiting for the person's OK (`held`, each with its
summary in full: the person agrees to what code wrote). `proposal_id` is the held proposal, null when nothing is
held; whether it can still be agreed to is `ChatConversationTurn.agree`.

WorkKind.title: WorkKind
WorkKind.description:
A kind of work a bench can have, from the skills config: its `name` (what `BenchSummary.work` holds) and the
`label` a screen shows.

WorkRequest.title: WorkRequest
WorkRequest.description:
A bench's kind of work: the `work` slug of one of `WorkshopKinds.work_kinds`, or null for none. A slug the
household has no kind for starts one, and then needs `label` (what to call it); a slug is lowercase letters, digits
and hyphens.

WorkshopKinds.title: WorkshopKinds
WorkshopKinds.description:
What a bench allows, so the client hard-codes none of it: the piece kinds, the size classes a piece may take
(`small` a quarter of the width, `medium` a half, `large` three quarters, `full` the row), the most pieces a bench
holds and the longest title of a bench or a piece; and the languages a code piece can be run in
(`run_languages`, empty while nothing can be run) and the longest body that can be run (`run_max_chars`).

Written.title: Written
Written.description: The generation the record holds after a write-back; the keeper's next carries it.

HTTPBearer.description: A device token from `python -m ashley.channels.devices add`.
